youtube.title: 🔥 Stop Burning Tokens - CodeGraph Cuts AI Agent Costs 16%
youtube.description:
Your AI coding agent is wasting your money. Every time Claude Code or Cursor explores your codebase, it spawns agents that grep files, read code, and burn through tokens just to understand what you already know.

CodeGraph fixes this by building a semantic knowledge graph of your entire codebase — symbol relationships, call graphs, and code structure — indexed locally in SQLite. When your agent needs to understand how a feature works, it queries the graph instead of reading thousands of files.

The results? Tested across 7 real-world codebases (Django, VS Code, Tokio, and more): 16% cheaper runs, 58% fewer tool calls, 22% faster answers, and near-zero file reads. Your agent answers architecture questions instantly instead of thrashing through grep and Read.

It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, opencode, Hermes Agent, Gemini, Antigravity, and Kiro. Supports 20+ languages including TypeScript, Python, Rust, Go, Java, and Swift. Completely local — no API keys, no cloud services, just one command to install and auto-wire your agents.

Next time you ask your agent 'How does this feature work?' it answers from the graph instead of spawning explore agents. Your token budget actually lasts, and you ship features faster.

Link in bio to install CodeGraph and stop paying for file exploration.

linkedin.text:
I just watched my AI coding agent burn $0.95 answering one architecture question.

The same question with CodeGraph? $0.57.

Here's what happened: Claude Code spawned explore agents to grep files, read code, and piece together how Alamofire processes HTTP requests. 12 tool calls, 2.1M tokens, 2 minutes 21 seconds.

With CodeGraph running? 5 tool calls, 766k tokens, 1 minute 35 seconds. Same answer. Zero file reads.

CodeGraph builds a semantic knowledge graph of your codebase — every symbol, every relationship, every call chain — indexed locally in SQLite. When your agent needs context, it queries the graph instead of spawning file exploration agents.

I tested this across 7 real-world codebases spanning 7 languages. Average savings: 16% cheaper, 47% fewer tokens, 22% faster, 58% fewer tool calls.

The pattern holds everywhere. VS Code (10k files): 81% fewer tool calls. Django (3k files): 77% fewer. Tokio, OkHttp, Gin, Excalidraw — CodeGraph cuts tool calls on every repo.

It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and 5 other agents. Supports 20+ languages. One command installs it and auto-wires your agents. Completely local — no API keys, no cloud, just a file watcher that keeps the graph fresh as you code.

Your AI agent is powerful. But every grep and Read costs tokens. CodeGraph gives it the context it needs upfront, so it answers instead of exploring.

Link in comments to try it. Your token budget will thank you.
